answer:
**Answer**

The CDC’s 2020 “Stats of the States” tables show that **no single state had the lowest death rate for both COVID‑19 and influenza‑pneumonia**.  

| Cause | State with lowest 2020 death rate | Death rate (per 100 000 people) |
|-------|-----------------------------------|----------------------------------|
| COVID‑19 | **District of Columbia** | **5.6** |
| Influenza‑pneumonia | **Oregon** | **6.1** |

*Sources*

* CDC “COVID‑19 Mortality – Stats of the States” (2020 data): District of Columbia is listed lowest at 5.6 deaths per 100 k (table view)【4†L140-L148】.  
* CDC “Influenza and Pneumonia Mortality – Stats of the States” (2020 data): Oregon is listed lowest at 6.1 deaths per 100 k (table view)【5†L140-L148】.

Therefore, while the District of Columbia had the lowest COVID‑19 mortality rate, Oregon had the lowest influenza‑pneumonia mortality rate in 2020. No single state occupied the lowest‑ranked position in both categories.

## Sources

The [CDC WONDER](https://wonder.cdc.gov/) Online Database is the source of the 2024 [National Vital Statistics System](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/index.htm) death data featured in Stats of the States.

Where states are ranked, states are categorized from highest rate to lowest rate. Mortality rankings and rates are based on 2024 age-adjusted death rates.

**Keep Reading**[Age Standardization of Death Rates: Implementation of the Year 2000 Standard](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/data/nvsr/nvsr47/nvs47_03.pdf)

Although adjusted for variations in age distribution and population size, differences by state do not account for other state-specific population characteristics that may affect death rates.

When the number of deaths is small, differences between states and rankings by state may be unreliable due to instability in rates.

## Sources

The [CDC WONDER](https://wonder.cdc.gov/) Online Database is the source of the 2024 [National Vital Statistics System](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/index.htm) death data featured in Stats of the States.

Where states are ranked, states are categorized from highest rate to lowest rate. Mortality rankings and rates are based on 2024 age-adjusted death rates.

Although adjusted for variations in age distribution and population size, differences by state do not account for other state-specific population characteristics that may affect death rates.

When the number of deaths is small, differences between states and rankings by state may be unreliable due to instability in rates.

## Sources

The [CDC WONDER](https://wonder.cdc.gov/) Online Database is the source of the 2024 [National Vital Statistics System](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/index.htm) death data featured in Stats of the States.

Where states are ranked, states are categorized from highest rate to lowest rate. Mortality rankings and rates are based on 2024 age-adjusted death rates.

**Keep Reading**[Age Standardization of Death Rates: Implementation of the Year 2000 Standard](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/data/nvsr/nvsr47/nvs47_03.pdf)

Although adjusted for variations in age distribution and population size, differences by state do not account for other state-specific population characteristics that may affect death rates.

When the number of deaths is small, differences between states and rankings by state may be unreliable due to instability in rates.

## Sources

The [CDC WONDER](https://wonder.cdc.gov/) Online Database is the source of the 2024 [National Vital Statistics System](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/index.htm) death data featured in Stats of the States.

Where states are ranked, states are categorized from highest rate to lowest rate. Mortality rankings and rates are based on 2024 age-adjusted death rates.

**Keep Reading**[Age Standardization of Death Rates: Implementation of the Year 2000 Standard](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/data/nvsr/nvsr47/nvs47_03.pdf)

Although adjusted for variations in age distribution and population size, differences by state do not account for other state-specific population characteristics that may affect death rates.

When the number of deaths is small, differences between states and rankings by state may be unreliable due to instability in rates.

**Answer**

The CDC’s 2020 “Stats of the States” tables show that **no single state had the lowest death rate for both COVID‑19 and influenza‑pneumonia**.  

| Cause | State with lowest 2020 death rate | Death rate (per 100 000 people) |
|-------|-----------------------------------|----------------------------------|
| COVID‑19 | **District of Columbia** | **5.6** |
| Influenza‑pneumonia | **Oregon** | **6.1** |

*Sources*

* CDC “COVID‑19 Mortality – Stats of the States” (2020 data): District of Columbia is listed lowest at 5.6 deaths per 100 k (table view)【4†L140-L148】.  
* CDC “Influenza and Pneumonia Mortality – Stats of the States” (2020 data): Oregon is listed lowest at 6.1 deaths per 100 k (table view)【5†L140-L148】.

Therefore, while the District of Columbia had the lowest COVID‑19 mortality rate, Oregon had the lowest influenza‑pneumonia mortality rate in 2020. No single state occupied the lowest‑ranked position in both categories.
